title: Hakawati: Free and Open Text-based RPG Client - Public Release
author: rakanssh
selftext:
Hello! Around a month ago I posted about a project I've been working on, a free and open-source text-based RPG client supporting both traditional AI-powered storytelling and an experimental gamemode where the AI tracks stats and inventory. It's finally ready for a public release!

I aim to continue working on it, hoping to eventually provide an experience comparable to commercial clients while giving users the freedom to use any model they want while paying for their actual usage/running on their own hardware.

The client is still in an early state, so expect some bugs, rough edges, and regular fixes. feel free to share any bugs you run into or feature requests you have using the [issue tracker](https://github.com/rakanssh/hakawati/issues).

The repository is [here on github](https://github.com/rakanssh/hakawati), with instructions on how to get started.

The latest release is available on the [releases page](https://github.com/rakanssh/hakawati/releases/latest):

* Linux (Get the .AppImage)
* MacOS (Get the .dmg installer)
* Windows (Get the .msi installer) The Windows build is not signed, not sure how to get it signed yet. Smartscreen may panic and try to block it with an unknown publisher warning. If you are concerned, you can follow the instructions in the README to build the client yourself from the source code on your own machine. I'd appreciate any tips on how to get a certificate as an individual.

comments.author: AssistBorn4589
comments.body:
I have slight issue with your description. I believe I can guess correctly what your application is, but to be sure:

By text-based RPG client, you mean RPG game which uses AI to progress? Or is it actual client for some specific RPG with AI features?

replies.author: rakanssh
replies.body: The former is more accurate, could have been worded better. It's a client in the sense that it relies on an external source for inference.

comments.author: GibtiGibti
comments.body: Looks great but didn´t recognize my ollama running.  Others like Msty do, so ollama works properly.

replies.author: rakanssh
replies.body:
Thanks!

The Ollama issue is likely CORS. I was able to get it working by following the[ instructions here ](https://objectgraph.com/blog/ollama-cors/)to allow all origins.

I'm working on a way to get it working without requiring the extra step, but for now following this and restarting Ollama (Make sure to kill the process) should let the app and any other browser based tool connect to your local Ollama.

replies.author: GibtiGibti
replies.body: The IP of my AI server shows "ollama running" in my browser. In Hakawati I only have OpenAI API in the settings to choose from. Used Msty for a while now and there it works under remote LLM.

replies.author: rakanssh
replies.body: Found a fix, an update should be out soon allowing it to work with and detect local tools without requiring extra CORS config. I'll push it once I've tested it to make sure nothing broke.
